summary: SC Forestry Commission fire tower in Pickens County, listed on a lookout-history site; no build date, height or fate found in any source read.

evidence.supports: Clemson record: South Carolina Forestry Commission
Lookout-history page gives only a name, county, agency and a satellite view
First SCFC fire tower erected near Camden, August 1930
evidence.quote: The first Forestry Commission fire tower was erected in August, 1930 near Camden.

evidence.supports: Most tower sites had 10 acres, the tower and a dwelling for the operator
evidence.quote: Most tower sites consisted of 10 acres of land, the tower, and a year-round dwelling for the operator.

evidence.supports: Network eventually included more than 130 towers
evidence.quote: The tower network eventually included more than 130 towers and was used for 65 years to detect wildfires.

evidence.supports: SCFC closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

evidence.supports: Post and Courier gives 1994 as the year the system was decommissioned
evidence.quote: The SCFC lookout tower system was decommissioned in 1994.

evidence.supports: Only 30 towers remain standing across the state (the article is undated in the copy read, so the story does not present this as current)
evidence.quote: Today, only 30 of them remain standing.

sources.title: Looking out for last fire towers

resolved_conflicts.explanation: SCFC's own history gives October 1, 1993 as the closure date; a Post and Courier item gives 1994 for decommissioning. The story uses the SCFC date and notes the 1994 date.

notes_for_editor: Only this record's lookout-history page and the statewide SCFC and Post and Courier pages were read, plus two searches. No build date, height, operator, status or site description for this tower was found. Coordinates in the source file (34.6274, -82.8429) put it about 13 km south of the NHLR-registered Issaqueena Tower (US 671, Clemson Experimental Forest, 34.74198, -82.83865). They are different towers; do not merge them. A place database entry 'Clemson Lookout Tower' (Oconee County) appeared in search results and was not read, so it is not used. Before publishing any fate or site-today line, check SCFC history records or Clemson University Forest staff. The Post and Courier last-towers article has no date in the copy read, so the story labels its 30-towers count as possibly out of date.
